the ionic conductivity in lithium borophasphate glass system is closely related to the structural variation induced by the glass former composition.
the conductivity of the lithium borophosphate system increases as the B 2 O/(B 2 O + P 5 O) ratio increases, and the maximum is achieved at B 2 O/P 5 O
the ionic conductivity of Li 2 B 4 O 7 glass is enhanced by the introduction of B 2O 3 and P 2O 5.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimum composition for the ionic conductivity is the glass composition with the highest concentration of 4-coordinating boron groups.
the ionic conductivity was strongly dependent on the network structure of the glasses, i.e. the ratio of 4-coordinating boron and 3-coordinating phosphorous.
the ionic conductivity was governed by the network structure and the ionic conductivity increased with increasing of the number of non-bridging oxygen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ionic conductivity of the Li 2 O-B 2 O 2 -P 2 O was maximized at a specific composition where the 4-coordinated BO 4 groups were maximized.
the ionic conduction in the Li 2 O-B 2 O 2 -P 2 O-5 glass is dominated by the boron network structure, which is in turn affected by the glass former composition.

the conductivity of the glass system was determined by the concentration of the 4-coordinated B groups, and that the maximum conductivity could be achieved at the specific concentration of the ionic groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ionic conductivity of the glass can be optimized by controlling the glass composition, and that the structural information of the glass network can be used to predict the ionic conductivity.
the ionic conductivity in the Li 2 O-rich glasses can be enhanced by increasing the 4-coordinated B groups.
the glass structure of Li 2 B 4 O 7 is an optimum structure to achieve the high ionic conductivity in the Li 2 O-B 2 O 2 -P 2 O system.
